reason: The text contains four named characters: Isaac (Yitzchak), Rebekah (Rivkah), Jacob (Ya'akov), and Esau ('Esav). While Isaac is clearly a patriarch and leader of his household, the other characters do not all qualify as leaders. Esau is portrayed primarily as a hunter who follows his father's instructions—he has the status of firstborn but is not depicted as a leader. Jacob at this point in the narrative is a younger son who employs deception; he is not yet established as a leader, though he will later become a patriarch. Rebekah, while exercising household authority and influence in orchestrating the blessing's deception, is not portrayed as a leader in the formal sense. Therefore, not all named characters are leaders, making the statement false.
